quote: Under the order of precedence, the Side Letter controls over the body of the Distribution Agreement. This means the six-state "Territory" in the Side Letter governs for purposes of the non-compete (§ 2.1 of the Side Letter). However, the four-state Territory in the Distribution Agreement still governs the exclusive appointment ... seek clarification or narrowing of the Side Letter's Territory definition to match the Distribution Agreement's four-state territory
reason: Issue 7 makes each required point. It says the Side Letter redefines Territory to add NY and VA. It says that definition controls under DA § 19.4's order of precedence. It says the non-compete therefore covers six states while exclusivity covers four. Issue 3 adds the 18-month post-term period. The memo also recommends conforming the definition to the four-state Territory. It does not suggest expanding exclusivity, but the criterion is satisfied by either remedy.
